reference.title: Dumbbell Side Bridge
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily through the hold; do not hold the breath.
breathing.cadence: About one breath every 3 s during the 9 s hold

prescription.holds: Short repeated holds (about 10 s) for beginners (clinical opinion)
prescription.progression: Longer holds, then lift the top leg or the top arm

cues.text: Lie on your right side, right elbow under the shoulder, forearm pointing forward, feet stacked, legs straight; hold a light dumbbell in the left hand.
Press the forearm into the mat and lift the hips until the body is one straight line; reach the dumbbell straight up to the ceiling.
Hips high and square, dumbbell stacked over the shoulder, arm straight, breathe steadily.
Keep the arm vertical and lower the hips to the mat under control.
Rest the dumbbell, then repeat; switch sides.

mistakes.fix: Lift the bottom hip; shorten the hold or bend the knees.
Keep the hips stacked, chest facing forward.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow out of line with the shoulder
Shoulder shrugged up to the ear
mistakes.fix: Push the floor away and draw the shoulder down.

mistakes.mistake: Dumbbell drifting toward the head or feet
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist stacked over the shoulder; a lighter dumbbell makes this easier.

kinematics.setup: Hips on the mat: trunk ≈27° off the leg line
kinematics.peak: ≈0° off straight (trunk vs legs); legs ≈163° up from the mat
kinematics.norm: Straight line from head through hips to feet (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: On the mat under the shoulder, forearm pointing forward
kinematics.peak: Directly under the shoulder, forearm pointing forward
kinematics.norm: Elbow directly under the shoulder, forearm on the floor (clinical opinion)
Hips rise until the side of the body is straight (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Dumbbell held straight up over the left shoulder
kinematics.peak: Within 9° of vertical through the whole set
kinematics.norm: Arm vertical, dumbbell stacked over the shoulder (clinical opinion)
Neutral, about 0 degrees in the hold (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s lift, 9 s hold with breathing settles, 1 s lower, 0.8 s rest
kinematics.norm: Isometric hold; side support gives high quadratus lumborum activity with modest spine load (McGill 1998)

sources.title: GymVisual #11396, Dumbbell Side Bridge, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Escamilla et al. 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765)

An electromyographic analysis of the Ab-Slide, abdominal crunch, supine double leg thrust and side bridge in healthy young adults (J Strength Cond Res 22(6):1939-1946, 2008; PubMed 18978615)

cautions: Use a light dumbbell and keep the wrist stacked over the shoulder; lower the dumbbell to the mat before lowering yourself if the arm tires (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shoulder pain on the supporting side (instability, rotator cuff): start with the knee side plank or skip.
modify: Bend the knees (knee side plank): about 40% less oblique activity (Escamilla 2016).
Stagger the feet (top foot in front) for balance.
regressions: Side plank without the dumbbell (top hand on the hip).

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Bottom-side obliques hold the trunk up against gravity; external oblique about 62% MVIC in the side bridge on the toes (Escamilla 2016) and 51% in Youdas 2008 (as summarised by St Mary's University). Recorded side not reported in these summaries.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Top-side obliques co-contract to keep the trunk straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Bottom-side hip abductors lift the pelvis off the mat; the side bridge was one of the exercises suggested for gluteus medius strengthening (above 45% MVIC, Ekstrom 2007).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Stands in for quadratus lumborum, which is highly active in side support (McGill 1998); lumbar paraspinals about 29% MVIC (Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis about 21-26% MVIC (Escamilla 2016); keeps the pelvis from tipping forward or back.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Top-side abductors keep the top leg stacked (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the supporting shoulder blade on the rib cage; the trunk must not sink between the shoulder blades.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the supporting shoulder over the elbow.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Steadies the supporting shoulder over the elbow.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff centres the supporting shoulder (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Draws the supporting shoulder down, away from the ear (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Top leg presses gently onto the bottom leg to keep the feet stacked (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Holds the top arm vertical under the dumbbell (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the top arm vertical under the dumbbell (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: steadies the top shoulder under the load (clinical opinion).

phases.label: On the right side, forearm down
